french: Comment forme-t-on le passé composé avec être ?
notes: Example: elle est allée. Non-reflexive verbs with être agree with the subject; reflexive agreement has additional rules.

french: Comment le participe passé s'accorde-t-il avec être ?
english: For non-reflexive verbs using être: it agrees with the subject in gender and number.
notes: elle est allée; ils sont partis; elles sont venues. Reflexive verbs have additional agreement rules.

french: Où place-t-on ne… pas au passé composé ?
english: Around the auxiliary: subject + ne/n' + auxiliary + pas + past participle.
notes: Je n'ai pas compris. Je ne suis pas allé(e).

french: Quelles sont les trois façons de poser une question au passé composé ?
notes: Tu es arrivé ? Es-tu arrivé ? Est-ce que tu es arrivé ?

french: Form the passé composé with avoir.
english: Present tense of avoir + past participle.
notes: J'ai regardé le spectacle.

french: Regular -er verbs: how do you form the past participle?
notes: aimer → aimé; chanter → chanté

french: Regular -ir verbs such as finir: past participle ending?
notes: finir → fini. This is not a rule for all -ir verbs: venir → venu.

french: Regular -re verbs such as vendre: past participle ending?
notes: vendre → vendu. Irregular examples: prendre → pris; faire → fait.

french: Complete: Elle ___ sortie. Elle ___ sorti son téléphone.
notes: She went out. She took out her phone. The second sentence has a direct object.
Feminine plural: -es.

french: A mixed group says: Nous sommes ___ (partir).
notes: Use masculine plural for a mixed group; parties for an all-female group.

french: Which auxiliary do reflexive verbs use in the passé composé?
notes: Je me suis habillé(e). Auxiliary choice alone does not determine every reflexive agreement.

french: Make negative: Nous avons regardé le programme.
english: Nous n'avons pas regardé le programme.

notes: Invert the auxiliary and subject pronoun.

french: How do you form the imparfait stem for most verbs?
english: Take the present-tense nous form and remove -ons.
notes: nous faisons → fais-; être is the exception.

french: What is the imparfait stem of être?
notes: It is not somm-.

french: Imparfait endings for je and tu?
notes: j'étais; tu étais

french: Imparfait ending for il / elle / on?
notes: il était; elle faisait; on chantait
nous étions; nous faisions
vous étiez; vous faisiez
ils étaient; elles faisaient

french: Complete in the imparfait: je ___ / nous ___ (manger).
notes: Keep e before a for the soft g sound; i already makes g soft.

french: Complete in the imparfait: je ___ / nous ___ (commencer).
notes: Use ç before a, but c before i.

french: Complete in the imparfait: il ___ / nous ___ (faire).
notes: Stem: fais-. The ai in these forms is pronounced /ə/.

french: Describe the background: « It was lively. »
Describe the background: « The weather was hot. »
Describe the background: « There were lots of people. »
english: Il y avait beaucoup de monde.

french: Make negative: Il y avait du monde.
english: Il n'y avait pas de monde.
notes: ne… pas surrounds avait; du becomes de after this negation.

french: Choose: Y avait-il / Y avait-t-il beaucoup de monde ?
notes: avait already ends in t; do not add another -t-.

french: Tu n'étais pas au concert ? Reply that you WERE there.
notes: Si contradicts a negative question or statement.

french: Which past tense normally describes a background state or an unbounded habit?
notes: Descriptions, weather, feelings, and ongoing actions when viewed as background.

french: Which past tense presents an event as a completed, bounded whole?
notes: It can also describe a completed number or period of repeated actions.

english: Je dormais quand le téléphone a sonné.
notes: Ongoing background + completed event.

french: Choose: Pendant une semaine, nous avons marché / marchions tous les jours. Present the week as a completed whole.
english: Pendant une semaine, nous avons marché tous les jours.
notes: Repetition does not automatically require the imparfait.

french: Is « Ça a été génial » grammatical?
english: Yes. It presents the experience as a completed whole.
notes: C'était génial normally describes the background or what it was like.

french: Which preposition follows jouer for games and sports?
english: à: jouer au tennis, jouer aux cartes
notes: à + le → au; à + les → aux

french: Which preposition follows jouer for instruments?
english: de: jouer du piano, jouer de la guitare
notes: de + le → du; de + la → de la

english: faire du jardinage / faire de la natation
notes: These activity expressions use faire de.

french: What does BAGS help you remember about French adjectives?
english: Common adjectives of beauty, age, goodness and size usually precede the noun.
notes: un beau costume; une jeune femme; un bon album; une petite robe
Use bel before a masculine singular noun beginning with a vowel or silent h.
Feminine: une vieille amie.
Feminine: une nouvelle chanson.
A simple colour adjective normally agrees in gender and number.
Marron, orange and crème are invariable colour adjectives.
Compound colour descriptions are invariable.

french: What is the difference between neuf and nouveau for an item of clothing?
english: Neuf means brand-new / unused; nouveau can mean newly acquired or different, even if used.
notes: Feminine: neuve / nouvelle.

french: Which means « wear », and which means « put on »: porter / mettre?
notes: Je porte une veste. Je vais mettre une veste.

french: Which verb form is used in written clothing-care instructions?
notes: Laver à la main. Vider les poches.

french: How do you write « Do not iron » as a care instruction?
notes: ne pas + infinitive; both negative words come before the verb.

english: Je connais Paris; je sais nager.
notes: connaître = familiarity with people, places or things; savoir + infinitive = know how to do something.

french: Complete: Je ___ que sa taille est 38.
english: Je sais que sa taille est 38.
notes: Use savoir for facts and information.

french: Why « après avoir utilisé le téléphone » rather than « après utiliser le téléphone »?
english: Après + past infinitive presents the action as completed before the next action.
notes: avoir utilisé = past infinitive, not a conjugated passé composé. « Faire une pause après avoir utilisé le téléphone. »
ne precedes the reflexive pronoun; pas follows the conjugated verb.

french: Translate: We are going to go for a walk.
notes: The reflexive pronoun stays immediately before the infinitive.

french: Make negative: Nous allons nous promener.
notes: Negation surrounds allons, not the infinitive.
-if → -ive.
Learn these separately; -oux has more than one feminine pattern.
The vocal cords vibrate for [v] and [z], but not for [f] and [s].
devoir + infinitive expresses obligation.
pouvoir + infinitive expresses ability or possibility.

french: Rewrite with est-ce que: Vous étudiez où ?
notes: Keep subject–verb order after est-ce que.
